**Problem statement**: A swarm of N agents (LLMs or models) each produce an answer/claim. Naive majority voting treats agreement as evidence of truth. But agents can be correlated: same training data, same prompt, shared context, copy-paste contamination, anchoring on an early output, etc. Correlated hallucination = N agents all wrong in the *same way* produces apparent consensus that is false. We need to detect when agreement is "true" (independent convergence on truth) vs "illusion" (correlated error).

Key insight from statistics: if errors were independent with per-agent error rate p, probability of k-out-of-N unanimous wrong answer is p^N — exponentially small. But with correlation ρ between agents' errors, P(all wrong) ≈ p·(1 + (N−1)ρ) roughly (for exchangeable Bernoulli via beta-binomial). So the detection task is to estimate effective independence and discount agreement accordingly.

### Sybil/bloc detection
If rosters are dynamic (agents join), bloc voting: many agents with near-identical outputs AND near-identical model fingerprints or timing. ### Merkle tree spec
Leaves: canonical CBOR of each record. Tree: binary, leaves padded to power-of-two by duplicating last leaf (Bitcoin-style) — or better, unbalanced-left-promotion? Pick: pad by repeating final leaf; depth = ceil(log2(L)); internal node = SHA256(0x01 || left || right); leaf = SHA256(0x00 || payload); single-leaf tree root = leaf hash. Empty set → SHA256(0x00). Sorted leaf order = canonical byte order of payloads. All sets mapped to leaves this way. Phase roots array in fixed order: [bundle, roster, answers, clusters, probes_stats, corr, reruns, verdict].

### Why two implementations agree — checklist
Enumerate every nondeterminism source and its kill switch:
1. Floats → banned; fixed point + integer log/exp algorithms.
2. Map/set iteration → canonical sorting everywhere.
3. Text normalization → frozen tables referenced by hash, NFC only.
4. RNG → ChaCha20 counter DRNG, domain-separated keys, rejection sampling spec'd.
5. Parallelism/races → sealed phases; aggregation consumes immutable sealed records; no shared mutable state enters hashing.
6. Library differences (JSON, unicode libs) → CBOR core deterministic; tables embedded.
7. Timing/env → no env reads; abort codes for missing inputs.
8. Model inference nondeterminism → decode params pinned (greedy or seeded per-agent DRNG nonce); model fingerprint recorded; if backend can't guarantee, its outputs still enter as opaque sealed text — the ROOT is over recorded outputs, so root determinism holds even if the underlying generation varies; but then the "same start" includes the transcripts. Important subtlety: byte-identical roots from same start requires the start to include all generated texts OR generation itself deterministic.
